title: Dynamic key-tiling and TTL synthesis for cost smoothing and safe rollout
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: produce a practical, automated recommendation engine and safe-apply/rollback playbook that tunes per-prefix/cache-key TTLs and coarse key-tiling (prefix grouping) to reduce token cost while keeping tail latency and error rate within SLOs. This ticket covers: hit-rate forecasting per logical key tile; an online TTL synthesis algorithm (Bayesian + gradient updates); cache-key selection heuristics for reducing cardinality without harming hit-rate; offline counterfactual simulation and a staged safety rollout with shadowing and automated rollback gates.
background: We currently have multiple TTL tuning and prefix-playbook tickets but no end-to-end recommender that balances cost, latency, and safety. Existing artifacts focus on per-prefix autotuning (see dependencies) but customers still face high unit-costs on long-tail prefixes and noisy key cardinality. This work aims to close the loop: model hit economics, propose tile+TTL candidates, simulate counterfactuals, and ship a conservative apply path with defined rollback criteria.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A reproducible offline simulator that predicts per-tenant monthly token spend delta within +/- 8% compared to actuals for held-out week. 2) Recommendation engine outputs TTL and tiling candidates for >90% of active prefixes with expected cost savings >= 10% on pilot dataset. 3) End-to-end rollout runbook (shadow -> canary -> ramp) documented and verified in staging with automated rollback triggers and a manual override. 4) No increase in 99th percentile latency above 5% during controlled canary. 5) PR with unit+integration tests and dashboard with per-prefix cost/hit-rate projections.
plan: Phase 0 - Discovery (1 week): gather prefix cardinality histograms, existing TTLs, upstream request traces, and token-cost attribution per model. Phase 1 - Modeling (2 weeks): build per-prefix/tile hit-rate forecasting using exponential smoothing + beta-binomial Bayesian update; compute expected cost vs TTL curve. Phase 2 - Tiling & Key-synthesis (2 weeks): design coarse 'tiling' (N-way bucketing) heuristics to reduce key cardinality while preserving hit-rate; generate candidate key transforms (truncate, hash-bucket, suffix-strip) and estimate collision risk. Phase 3 - Simulator & Counterfactuals (2 weeks): implement replay-based simulator with shadow sampling to compute cost/latency tradeoffs and risk metrics. Phase 4 - Safety Gates & Rollout Automation (2 weeks): implement staged apply pipeline (shadow -> staged canary -> regional ramp) with automated enforcer that aborts or rolls back based on cost uplift, hit-rate degradation, and latency tail shifts. Phase 5 - Pilot and Iterate (4 weeks): run on internal non-critical namespace, capture learnings, and prepare customer rollout guidance.
instrumentation: Metrics to add: per-key and per-tile: requests/sec, distinct key cardinality, hits, misses, hit_rate, avg_prefix_ttl, time_to_first_miss, served_tokens, total_cost_estimate. Derived health signals: delta_cost_estimate, hit_rate_trend_7d, p50/p95/p99 latency for cached vs uncached, collision_rate (for tiled keys). Dashboards: 'tiling-synth dashboard', 'ttl-recommender projection', and an 'apply-safety' dashboard showing live canary thresholds. Logs: candidate transform id, rollout id, observed vs predicted hit_rate, and mismatch reasons.
recommendation_engine_design: Input: recent request traces + current TTLs + model token-cost profile. Step A: aggregate request keys into candidate tiles by frequency quantiles and semantic grouping (route, model, tenant). Step B: for each tile estimate a hit-curve by simulating TTL sweep (analytical approx via Poisson arrival + beta posterior for hit probability). Step C: compute marginal cost reduction vs added miss-cost and estimate tail-latency risk via sampled request traces. Step D: output prioritized list of (tile, transform, proposed_ttl, expected_savings, risk_score). Risk scoring combines sample variance of hit-rate, tail-latency delta, and customer-impact tag. Use conservative priors for low-volume tiles.
tiling_and_key_design_notes: - Prefer deterministic, reversible transforms so we can map errors back and safely rollback. - When tiling, avoid mixing high-variance tenants with stable system traffic; maintain tenant isolation buckets. - Provide 'collision mitigation' fallback that maps collided keys to a secondary namespace with short TTL. - Add metadata tags to recommended transforms for explainability (why this tile, what fraction of cost reduced).
simulator_spec: Replay engine should support: 1) deterministic replay of production traces over a synthetic TTL policy; 2) sampling-based shadowing to run candidate policies in parallel on live traffic (no write-through) for 48-72 hours; 3) counterfactual cost/latency estimation with confidence intervals; 4) ability to inject spike scenarios (x5 qps) to validate tail behavior. Output: per-candidate expected monthly cost delta, 95% CI, expected p99 delta, and 'rollback probability' under stress.
rollout_plan: Step 0: Create pilot set (10-20 tiles) that account for 40% of current cache spend. Step 1 (Shadow 72h): run candidate transforms in shadow for 72 hours, verify predictions within tolerance. Step 2 (Canary 1% traffic, 48h): enable 'read' caching with candidate TTLs for small fraction; monitor safety gates. Step 3 (Canary 10% traffic, 72h): expand if gates pass. Step 4 (Regional ramp): 25% -> 50% -> 100% over days with auto abort if any gate trips. Step 5 (Postmortem & full rollout): runbook completion and documentation. All rollout actions must create an audit log and link to rollout-id in dashboard.
rollback_triggers: observed hit_rate drop > 8% absolute for any tile for 30m
application error rate increase > 0.5% absolute or relative spike > 3x baseline
safety_controls: - Start with conservative TTL reductions (max 2x reduction for high-impact tiles). - Automated rollback on any trigger. - Manual gating for tenant-tagged high-impact customers. - Canary time windows with synthetic spike tests. - Shadow mode with persisted metrics for 7 days before manual approval. - Automated 'undo' transform that restores previous TTLs and key mapping immutably via a rollback-id.
deliverables: runbook for safe apply and rollback
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: misestimation on low-volume tails leading to cost regressions -> Mitigation: conservative priors and require higher sample thresholds before apply
Risk: key collisions after tiling causing cache thrash -> Mitigation: collision detection metric, short TTL fallback and automatic un-tiling
Risk: hidden customer-impact from tenant mixing -> Mitigation: tenant-isolation constraint and manual approval for tenant-bound tiles
Risk: simulator overfits historical traffic patterns -> Mitigation: run spike-in experiments and keep 20% of traffic as a live validation set
